description: Establishment of 50 MW Battery Energy Storage Systems
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-03-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In recent years, it is observed that, although Sri Lanka has experienced a rapid growth in renewable energy capacity, current system observations have identified that peak night-time demand is increasing approximately 2 years earlier than anticipated in the approved Long-Term Generation Expansion Plan. In order to improve the flexibility of the power system and increase the use of renewable energy, the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka has approved the commissioning of the 300 MW Battery Energy Storage System capacity, which was initially planned for the period 2031-2032, during the period 2028-2029 under the Long-Term Power Generation Plan. Accordingly, out of the approved 300 MW Battery Energy Storage System capacity, 250 MW has been decided to be procured through 25 projects of installing 10 MW/40 MWh standalone Battery Energy Storage Systems directly connected to the medium voltage distribution network of the Ceylon Electricity Board. The remaining 50 MW of Battery Energy Storage System capacity is expected to be procured through the connection of Battery Energy Storage Systems with existing ground-mounted solar power plants through a competitive bidding process. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to implement the relevant procurement process for the procurement of the proposed 50 MW Battery Energy Storage System capacity through the Renewable Energy Procurement & Performance Monitoring Division of National System Operator (Pvt) Ltd., a successor company of the Ceylon Electricity Board, was approved by the Cabinet.
